evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Transformer-based language models a monotonic decline in out-of-distribution reasoning accuracy after exceeding the critical threshold, rather than a simple flattening]

[PATH:empirical] Controlled scaling experiments on OOD reasoning benchmarks (e.g., BIG-Bench, MMLU, or synthetic compositional reasoning tasks) with systematic variation of model size and training data size, measuring accuracy at multiples of the critical threshold. — Directly tests the monotonic decline prediction by observing accuracy trends when model capacity exceeds the threshold by 2x or more, controlling for data fixedness.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of capacity-regularization trade-offs in transformer models, e.g., using the double-descent or grokking literature to derive conditions under which OOD accuracy degrades monotonically past a critical capacity point. — Provides mechanistic understanding of whether monotonic decline is a necessary consequence of overparameterization on fixed data, or if flattening is theoretically plausible.

qualifier.condition: when training data is held fixed and the threshold is exceeded by at least 2x

C006.subject: Transformer-based language models
C006.object: consistent improvements in reasoning capabilities with increased training compute
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Transformer-based language models consistent improvements in reasoning capabilities with increased training compute]

[PATH:empirical] Controlled scaling experiments on arithmetic reasoning benchmarks (e.g., GSM8K, MATH) with transformer models of varying parameter counts and training FLOPs, controlling for data quality and architecture. — Directly tests the hypothesis by isolating compute as a variable and measuring reasoning performance, providing quantitative evidence for or against monotonic improvement.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of scaling laws for reasoning tasks, e.g., extending Kaplan et al. (2020) or Hoffmann et al. (2022) to predict reasoning-specific loss or accuracy as a function of compute. — Provides a formal framework to predict whether reasoning improvements follow smooth scaling or exhibit diminishing returns, helping to adjudicate the disputed claim.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of published results from major language model evaluations (e.g., BIG-Bench, MMLU, ARC) across different compute regimes, including models from GPT-3, PaLM, Chinchilla, and LLaMA families. — Synthesizes existing empirical evidence to detect trends and outliers, addressing reproducibility and potential confounds like data contamination or benchmark saturation.

C007.subject: Transformer-based language models
C007.object: diminishing returns in reasoning capability at high training compute when using adaptive data curricula that prioritize novelty over coherence
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Transformer-based language models diminishing returns in reasoning capability at high training compute when using adaptive data curricula that prioritize novelty over coherence]

[PATH:empirical] Controlled scaling experiments with transformer LMs (e.g., 1B to 100B parameters) using adaptive curricula that vary novelty threshold (0.5–0.9) while measuring reasoning benchmarks (e.g., GSM8K, MATH, BBH). — Directly tests whether reasoning gains per compute unit decline above a novelty threshold of 0.7, isolating the effect of coherence loss.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of data distribution shifts under novelty-based selection, using information-theoretic bounds on generalization error for transformer training with non-i.i.d. curricula. — Provides a formal framework to predict when novelty-driven curricula cause diminishing returns by reducing sample efficiency due to fragmented or incoherent training sequences.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of existing literature on curriculum learning for LLMs (e.g., ACL/NeurIPS 2022–2025 papers on data selection strategies), focusing on results that compare novelty-based vs. coherence-based or mixed curricula. — Synthesizes prior evidence to identify whether reported scaling trends align with the hypothesized diminishing returns, especially at high compute regimes.

scope.domain: curriculum learning with dynamic data selection

qualifier.condition: if data diversity scales with compute but novelty selection threshold exceeds 0.7
